segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And its fortress and its wall and many of the courts and baths in it were overthrown,
and about fifty thousand souls died under the ruins.
Its lord, however, escaped,
because he happened to be outside in a garden.
And he put on sackcloth and sat upon ashes,
because of the great grief (or sorrow?) that had happened.
And he departed and went and fortified himself in one of his fortresses,
through fear of the Ghuzz,
those who had also gained dominion over Khwarazm.
And over Khorasan arose as chief
Ibrahim son of Yusuf, the uterine brother of Toghril Beg.
This man wrote a letter and sent it with an envoy to Baghdad, and spoke in it thus:
"The great Shahanshah,
that is, the king of kings, Toghril Beg the Seljuk, has been made king over Khorasan and Khwarazm,
and he is prepared to send an army to Baghdad,
because he has heard what the Ma'addites are doing on the pilgrimage route,
and how they take captive and plunder those who go to worship in the House of God.
Therefore, see to it
that with honours and gifts you meet his forces,
so that he may cause peace to reign over all the inhabited world."
Now he had drawn at the head of the letter the figure of a bow and an arrow.
And in this year hail fell of one and two Baghdad litras [in weight],
and it destroyed more than thirty villages in the region of Baghdad.
And in the year 1354
1354 of the Greeks [1042-1043 AD],
a certain rebel among the Romans went forth whose name was Maniaces (or Maniakes?),
and about twenty thousand men joined him.
Then King Constantine sent against him Christopher the eunuch with forty thousand men,
and he defeated the rebel,
and killed him, and set his head upon a reed.
And he mounted upon donkeys two hundred of the rebel's force bound in chains,
with their faces toward the tails of the donkeys.
And between the eyes of each one of them he hung four testicles of the slain, and the windpipe of the lungs, and the liver.
And heralds proclaimed before them in the streets of the imperial city:
"This is the just reward of everyone who rebels against the king."
And when he had mocked them,
the king had mercy upon them,
and did not kill them,
but dismissed them and said,
"Go wherever you wish."
To his soldiers, however, the king gave gifts,
of seventy dinars [each],
and of thirty-five,
for their victory.
